summary: Iteration 1 fully resolved the reported bug: a preemption-driven double-counting error was inflating total_output_tokens by up to 9.1% (9,548 tokens on 265 preemptions). The fix—subtracting already-counted output tokens at preemption time and resetting TTFT/ITL state—produces identical token counts (105,082) across all KV cache sizes, and a new regression test passes.
key_points: Bug confirmed and fixed: pre-fix, 265 preemptions inflated total_output_tokens from 105,082 to 114,630 (+9.1%); post-fix, all three KV cache sizes (600, 6,000, 60,000 blocks) produce exactly 105,082.

Root cause was ProgressIndex reset to 0 in batch_formation.go:232 causing decode-loop increments in simulator.go:647 to re-count tokens from restarted requests; fix stores OutputTokensGenerated before the reset and subtracts it in the preemption handler.

Two open questions remain: (1) whether ITL percentile metrics (P90/P95/P99) are now accurate under preemption (ITL array is reset but not explicitly tested at the aggregate level), and (2) whether cluster-level TTFTSum aggregation in cluster/cluster.go:1274 correctly propagates the per-instance fix across multi-instance deployments.
All existing sim/ tests pass; the only known test failure (TestFetchHFConfig_Success in cmd/) is a pre-existing, unrelated httptest panic.

Recommendation: the core total_output_tokens correctness question is fully answered; a follow-up iteration would be warranted only to validate ITL percentile accuracy and cluster-level TTFT aggregation under preemption.
